subject: DPA: definitions and carve-outs for training / model improvement
messages:
From: Dana Cole <procurement@infrahealth.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: Mark Reyes <mark.reyes@infrahealth.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redline: request to prohibit training on customer data

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. InfraHealth has reviewed the standard Redwood DPA and we've attached a redline with a request that customer data not be used for training or model improvement under any circumstances.

Key asks in our redline:
- Add a clear definition of "Model Training" and explicitly exclude any use of Customer Data for model development, fine-tuning, evaluation, or improving models;
- A carve-out that allows Redwood to use only aggregated anonymized telemetry for service maintenance (we proposed tight language around thresholds and irreversibility);
- Confirmation of subprocessor list and an explicit clause requiring prior notice and right to object for new subprocessors processing personal data in the EU;
- DocuSign execution preferred; InfraHealth legal would like a two-week turnaround on final DPA.

Attached: InfraHealth_DPA_redline.pdf (redline with inline comments).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the non-training carve-out as proposed, or if you have alternative language that would be acceptable? If helpful, we can schedule a quick call with our counsel (Mark) tomorrow afternoon.

Best,
Dana Cole
Senior Procurement Manager
InfraHealth Systems

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: Mark Reyes <mark.reyes@infrahealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redline: request to prohibit training on customer data

Hi Dana —

Thanks for the redline and clear asks. We understand the importance of this for InfraHealth and appreciate the proposed carve-out. Two quick points up-front:

1) Redwood's standard practice is to offer a "no-training" commitment for customers on contract in regulated sectors; we typically capture this as an explicit paragraph in Section 3 (Data Use) and specify permitted service maintenance telemetry separately.
2) We need to align on definitions (e.g., "Model Training", "Aggregated Anonymized Telemetry") to avoid ambiguity during operations and audits.

I've looped in Ben (account lead) and Laura (legal) to suggest specific alternative language that preserves InfraHealth's prohibition on training while allowing Redwood to continue safe maintenance and monitoring. Laura, Ben — can you review the attached bullet in-line language and LMK if you'd like to propose redline text?

Proposed next step: short call Monday 4/20 10am PT to finalize language and confirm DocuSign workflow. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks —
Soojin Lee
Sr. Account Executive, Healthcare
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 19 Apr 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redline: request to prohibit training on customer data

Ben / Soojin —

I reviewed InfraHealth's redline. High level: we're willing to accept a firm "no training" commitment but need to make the operational carve-outs narrow and auditable. Suggested approach (high level):

- Define "Model Training" as any use of Customer Data to derive model weights, hyperparameter tuning, gradient updates, or to build models for general-purpose use.
- Insert explicit carve-out: Redwood may process de-identified, aggregated telemetry solely for system stability, security, and performance monitoring, where such telemetry cannot be reverse-engineered to re-identify customer content. Example metrics: token throughput by region, error rates, latency percentiles.
- Add a 30-day prior-notice plus right-to-object mechanism for adding new subprocessors — if InfraHealth objects, we will either (a) remove the subprocessor for their account or (b) negotiate additional controls (SCCs, DPA amendment).
- For DocuSign: we'll prepare the final DPA and route for signature. I recommend adding a contract term that the no-training commitment survives termination for 24 months.

Proposed clause (for insertion):
"Customer Data shall not be used by Redwood for model training, model improvement, or model development (collectively, 'Model Training'). Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may process Aggregated Telemetry that is rendered irreversible and cannot be used to reconstruct or infer Customer Data, solely for the purpose of system maintenance, reliability and security, provided that such processing does not result in Model Training as defined above."

I'll attach the redline with tracked changes. If Ben and Soojin are aligned, I'll finalize and send to Dana for signature.

- Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Legal — Privacy & Data Protection
Redwood Inference

Hi Dana / Mark —

Thanks for the call this morning — appreciated the productive conversation. Per our agreed edits, Redwood has accepted the proposed non-training commitment with the clarified definitions and the narrow maintenance telemetry carve-out Laura proposed. We also agreed the commitment will survive termination for 24 months.

I attached the finalized DPA redline and routed the execution via DocuSign. Please review the executed copy once you receive the signature request. The DocuSign envelope is live here: https://app.docusign.com/exec?doc=DH-4839&env=prod (Envelope: DH-4839).

Summary of agreed items:
- "Model Training" explicitly prohibited as defined in Section 2.1;
- "Aggregated Telemetry" carve-out permitted exclusively for reliability, security, and performance monitoring;
- 30-day prior notice plus right to object for new subprocessors;
- No-training commitment survives termination for 24 months;
- DocuSign execution path; Redwood counter-signed and sent to InfraHealth for signature.

Attachments: InfraHealth_DPA_redline.pdf (original), Redwood_revised_DPA_redline.pdf (final redline), InfraHealth_DPA_executed_docusign.pdf (signed copy once InfraHealth signs).

Let me know if you need anything else — Ben and I will follow up on onboarding steps after signatures are complete.
